cues.text: Watch F1 Finance's accounting machine reconcile October's bank account for HANGS Construction.
A bank reconciliation matches the books to the bank statement, line by line.
First it reads the statement, the cash register and the ledger, and checks that each one adds up.
Next it ties the opening balances to September's signed reconciliation, and follows up the items left open then.
Now it looks for every deposit in the books on the bank statement.
One deposit, of $25,000, hasn't reached the bank yet.
One check cleared for $27 more than recorded: two digits were swapped.
Then it adds what only the bank knew about: its fees and the interest it paid.
The adjusted bank and book balances now agree to the cent: a $0.00 difference.
It proposes three small entries, about $70 net, and writes the workpapers and memo.
All done. The account reconciles to the cent at about $1.03 million, with five open items. Nothing was posted; the controller reviews and signs.
Jumping to the results. A person still reviews every item before anything is posted, paid or sent.
